76-001.r: Communal Award → issued by British PM Ramsay MacDonald (16 August), after Second RTC reached no consensus on separate electorates for Depressed Classes and communities.

76-002.r: Communal Award (16 August 1932, Ramsay MacDonald) → first gave a separate electorate to Untouchables (Depressed Classes), who could also vote in general constituencies.

76-004.r: Communal Award (16 August 1932) → separate electorates for Muslims, Depressed Classes, Indian Christians, Sikhs, Anglo-Indians and others; not for Buddhists.

76-005.r: Gandhi's first fast unto death → 20 September 1932, Yerwada Jail, against Communal Award; Poona Pact 24 September; fast ended 26 September 1932.

76-008.r: Seats for depressed classes in provincial legislatures: Communal Award 71 → Poona Pact 148 (some books say 147); book answer: 71 and 147. Poona Pact concerned untouchables' representation.

76-011.r: Poona Pact (24 September 1932, Gandhi-Ambedkar) defeated Communal Award's purpose → joint electorate with reserved seats, paving way for SC/ST reservation → both true, R explains A.

76-013.r: Poona Pact (24 September 1932), after Gandhi's fast against Communal Award → signed by Gandhi's followers and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; Gandhi himself did not sign.
76-013.c: Answer not printed (*); option 'Gandhiji and Ambedkar' fits loosely, but explanation says Gandhi did not sign.

76-015.r: Poona Pact (24 September 1932) → signed by Ambedkar (depressed classes), Madan Mohan Malviya (Hindus), Rajagopalachari and others; M.K. Gandhi did not sign.
76-015.t: Pact is called Gandhi-Ambedkar, but Gandhi never signed the document.

76-016.r: Harijan Sevak Sangh (earlier All India Anti-Untouchability League, founded by Gandhi in 1932 after Poona Pact) → first President Ghanshyam Das Birla.

76-017.r: After Poona Pact (1932) Gandhi made Harijan upliftment an all-India programme → Harijan Sevak Sangh (30 September 1932), weekly 'Harijan', Harijan tours; first President G.D. Birla.

76-021.r: Harijan Sevak Sangh → organised by Mahatma Gandhi (as All India Anti-Untouchability League, 1932); weekly 'Harijan' 1933; G.D. Birla first President.
76-021.t: Founder: Gandhi; first President: G.D. Birla.

76-022.r: All India Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932) → founded by Mahatma Gandhi to eradicate untouchability.

76-023.r: Former name of Harijan Sevak Sangh → All India Anti-Untouchability League (founded by Gandhi, 30 September 1932).

76-024.r: All India Depressed Classes League → Babu Jagjivan Ram; All India Scheduled Caste Federation → B.R. Ambedkar (1942); All India Depressed Classes Association → M.C. Rajah (1926).

76-025.r: 'Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not the level' → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to Gandhi, Mumbai, 14 August 1931.

77-001.r: Congress Socialist Party → formed May 1934 at Patna (first meeting); its policies settled at Bombay, October 1934.

77-003.r: Congress Socialist Party formed at Patna in 1934 (not January); J.P. Narayan General Secretary; Jawaharlal Nehru did not formally join → neither statement correct.

77-004.r: Congress Socialist Party (1934): socialist caucus within Congress, influenced by Fabianism and Marxism, for decentralised socialism → none of the three statements correct.

77-005.r: Congress Socialist Party (October 1934) → formed by Acharya Narendra Dev and Jaya Prakash Narayan.

77-007.r: All India Congress Socialist Party, Patna 1934 → convenor and General Secretary Jaya Prakash Narayan; President Acharya Narendra Dev; Ashok Mehta a founder member.

77-010.r: Bihar Socialist Party (1931) → formed by Phulan Prasad Varma at his home, with J.P. Narayan (book answer), Gangasharan Sinha, Rambriksh Benipuri, Ramanand Mishra.

77-013.r: 'Loknayak' → Jayaprakash Narayan; underground Quit India work (1942); declared 'Sampoorna Kranti' at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, 5 June 1974; Bharat Ratna posthumously 1999.

77-016.r: Jaya Prakash Day → April 1946, rally at Bankipur Maidan, Patna, demanding J.P. Narayan's release from prison.

77-017.r: Bombay Manifesto (1936, signed by 21 businessmen) → openly attacked Nehru's socialist preaching at Lucknow; widely backed by business community → both true.

78-001.r: 1937 elections (Government of India Act 1935): Congress full majority in 5 provinces (Madras, Bihar, CP and Berar, U.P., Orissa); not in Bengal, Punjab, Sindh.

78-005.r: 1937: Congress ministries in Madras, CP, Bihar, Bombay, Orissa, U.P. (July 1937); none in Bengal and Punjab.

78-006.r: 1937 elections → Congress lacked absolute majority in Bombay and Assam; did not form a ministry in Bengal.
78-006.c: Answer not printed (*); explanation names two options, Bombay and Assam.

78-008.r: 1937: Congress full majority in 5 provinces; ministries in 6 (July 1937: Bombay, U.P., CP, Orissa, Bihar, Madras), later coalitions in NWFP and Assam; none in Punjab.
78-008.c: Answer not printed (*); UPPSC did not evaluate it; count is 6 at first, more with later coalitions.

78-010.r: Congress ministries (1937) lasted 28 months → resigned 22 October 1939 over India's entry into Second World War without consent; League's 'Day of Deliverance' 22 December 1939.

78-013.r: Shri Krishna Singh, Bihar Premier (cabinet 20 July 1937), resigned February 1938 to press the Governor to release political prisoners; resumed after Governor agreed.

78-014.r: Congress Working Committee 1937 → adopted policy of abolishing feudal intermediaries (land ownership); tenancy bills passed in U.P. and Bihar.

78-015.r: U.P. ministry 1937 (Congress won 134 of 228 seats): Premier G.B. Pant; Finance → Rafi Ahmed Kidwai; Law and Justice → Kailash Nath Katju.

78-016.r: Reports on Muslim grievances under Congress ministries: Pirpur Report (1938) → Sharif Report (March 1939) → Fazlul Haq's 'Muslim sufferings' report (December 1939).

78-017.r: First Governor of Bihar (separated from Orissa, 1936, under 1935 Act) → Sir James David Sifton (1 April 1936 to 10 March 1937).

79-001.r: 1938 Congress President → Subhash Chandra Bose, unopposed, Haripura Session (Gujarat, February 1938); re-elected at Tripuri 1939 defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

79-004.r: Tripuri (1939 session) → Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh; Bose beat Pattabhi Sitaramayya by 1580 votes to 1377.

79-005.r: Bose's second presidency → Tripuri Session 1939 (beat Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya); first: Haripura 1938; after Bose resigned, Rajendra Prasad became President.
79-005.h: H comes before T: Haripura first, Tripuri second.

79-012.r: Bose-right wing dispute after the Tripuri Session → formation of Congress Working Committee.

79-013.r: Subhash Chandra Bose saw a Germany-Britain war as a godsend opportunity, citing Irish saying 'Need of England is an opportunity for Ireland'.

80-001.r: Butler Committee (1927, Sir Harcourt Butler) → to clarify relationship between the Paramount Power (Crown) and Princely States.

80-002.r: All India States People's Conference → December 1927; over 1500 workers; Balwant Rai Mehta, Manilal Kothari, G.R. Abhyankar key figures.

80-003.r: President of All India States Peoples Conference in 1939 → Jawaharlal Nehru.

80-004.r: Most princely states integrated in 1947 under Sardar Patel; Junagarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Hyderabad delayed, made to join by end of 1948.

80-007.r: Jammu and Kashmir joined India → 26 October 1947: Maharaja Hari Singh signed Instrument of Accession; Indian Army entered 27 October 1947.

80-008.r: At Partition, Punjab offered a plan for united, independent existence; Patel's efforts created PEPSU (Eastern Punjab, Patiala and hill States) instead.

80-009.r: Standstill Agreement (29 November 1947) → Hyderabad (Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan) and Dominion of India (Lord Mountbatten).

80-010.r: Parallel movement in princely states (Kashmir, Hyderabad, Travancore) from 1920s → Praja Mandal Movement (State People's Conference).

81-001.r: Congress policy in Second World War (1939) → would cooperate with Britain only on assurance of Complete Independence; India made belligerent without consultation.

81-002.r: Congress did not assist Britain in Second World War; it would not fight for democracy while India was denied freedom → both S and R false.

81-003.r: Lord Linlithgow declared India at war with Germany (3 September 1939) without consent → Congress ministries resigned in 1939 → A and R true, R explains A.
